cbpVsQcewReason: Both count jobs, differently: QCEW is an annual average of monthly employment covered by unemployment insurance, from employer filings; CBP is employment in the pay period including March 12 at establishments with payroll, with noise infusion. Levels differ systematically — compare direction of change, not levels.

basket.basis: Fish farms and hatcheries. QCEW covers employers; the Census of Agriculture (ag_aquaculture_farms, ag_aquaculture_sales) counts operations and sales, including those with no employees, and is the better count.
Finfish and shellfish fishing. Great Lakes commercial licences are few; the industry is still wholly water.
Water supply and irrigation (22131), sewage treatment (22132), steam (22133). The last is not water economy but is not separable in county data; a known overcount, small.
Processing of fish and shellfish. Downstream of fishing and aquaculture; wholly dependent on them.
Ship building and repair (336611), boat building (336612). The whole industry makes vessels.
Inland and Great Lakes shipping, freight and passenger (NAICS 4831 deep sea, coastal and Great Lakes; 4832 inland). The whole industry is on the water.
Tour boats, charters, dinner cruises. The whole industry is on the water.
Port and harbor operations, marine cargo handling, navigational services, salvage. Exists only because vessels call.
Docking, storage and services for pleasure craft. The whole industry is on the water.
